# Function Declarations

## Named Function Declarations

[Every parameter of a named function is written with its type](#spec.functions.named-function-declarations.legality-2) (a receiver excepted), and the checker never infers a named declaration's signature from its body or its callers. The return type follows `->`; [a function with no return annotation and no `return expr;` returns `()`](#spec.functions.named-function-declarations.dynamics-1). `return expr;` and bare `return;` are both valid. A closure, by contrast, infers its parameter and return types ([Closures](closures/index.md#closures)).

[A body whose value is not `()` under a signature with no `->`](#spec.functions.named-function-declarations.dynamics-1) is an ordinary type mismatch, [T0001](../../error-codes.md#t0001--type-mismatch), whose help line names the fix: write `-> T`, or, for a private function that captures nothing, calls no other function recursively and needs no generics, bind a closure instead.

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.named-function-declarations.legality-1}

Named function declarations begin with `fun`; `fun` is not an anonymous-function
expression introducer.

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.named-function-declarations.legality-2}

A named function declaration writes the type of each of its parameters, a receiver (`self`,
`&self`, `&var self`) excepted; an omitted parameter type is
[T0010](../../error-codes.md#t0010--unannotated-declaration). Its return type is written after
`->`, or is `()` when there is none: the checker does not infer a named declaration's
signature from its body or from its callers. This holds for free functions (private or
`pub`), methods and aspect-method declarations. `native` functions are unchanged. A
closure's parameter and return types are not subject to this rule.

##### Dynamic Semantics {#spec.functions.named-function-declarations.dynamics-1}

A function with no return annotation and no `return expr;` returns `()`.

## Local Functions

A `fun` declared inside a function body is a local function. It is an item, not a value with an environment: [its body sees its own parameters, locals and type parameters, module-level items, and the items declared in enclosing blocks, and does not see the locals or type parameters of the enclosing function](#spec.functions.local-functions.legality-1). What needs an environment is a closure ([Closures](closures/index.md#closures)): it names what it captures and the closure rules check it.

<!-- doc-example: expect-fail reason="rejected form: a local function does not capture (the first statement is the error)" -->
```metel
fun main() {
    var n := 0;
    fun bump() { n += 1; }                      // error[T0003]: `bump` is a function and cannot use `n`, a local of `main`
    let bump_closure := [&var n] var || { n += 1; };   // a closure captures
}
```

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.local-functions.legality-1}

The body of a function declared in a block sees: its own parameters, locals and type parameters;
module-level items, types, aspects and constants; and the items declared in enclosing blocks, such
as sibling local functions and local types. It does not see the locals of an enclosing function,
meaning its parameters, its `let` and `var` bindings, the receiver `self` and a closure's
captures, nor the enclosing function's type parameters. Naming one of these from the body is
[T0003](../../error-codes.md#t0003--undefined-name), with a note that the name is a local of the
enclosing function and the two fixes, binding a closure or passing the value as a parameter; for a
type parameter the note says to declare it on the local function. Local functions are hoisted
like any other ([scoping-and-shadowing.legality-3](../declarations/variables/scoping-and-shadowing.md#spec.declarations.variables.scoping-and-shadowing.legality-3)).

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

## Program Entry Point

[The root module must declare exactly one function named `main`](#spec.functions.program-entry-point.legality-1), callable with zero
arguments, with a body the type checker can type. This is a purely static, declarative
fact — answerable from the declaration table alone, with no dependency on program
execution — and a violation is a compile-time error, not a runtime one.

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.program-entry-point.legality-1}

The root module declares exactly one function named `main`, non-generic, callable with
zero arguments, with a body the type checker can type. Violating this is a compile-time
error, not a runtime one.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 4b7cdfbce41631b5c474a96ef9ceee8b4f81ef7a -->

## Associated Functions

`extend` blocks may contain functions with no `self` parameter. [These are called on
the type via `::` syntax](#spec.functions.associated-functions.legality-1) and serve as
the canonical constructor pattern:

```metel
struct Point {
    x: f64,
    y: f64,
}

extend Point {
    fun new(x: f64, y: f64) -> Point {
        return Point { x = x, y = y };
    }
}

fun main() -> i64 {
    let p := Point::new(1.0, 2.0);
    return p.x as i64;
}
```

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.functions.associated-functions.legality-1}

A function declared in an `extend` block without a `self`, `&self`, or `&var self`
parameter is an associated function and is called through its target type with `::`.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->
